title: Ben Carroll adds artificial intelligence ministry to Victorian cabinet, dumps transport infrastructure
full_text:
New Victorian premier Ben Carroll has announced the make-up of his new cabinet, including a new ministry dedicated to ethical and responsible artificial intelligence development.
Ally of former premier Jacinta Allan, Jaclyn Symes, has lost the treasury to Colin Brooks, who will also take on industrial relations.
Ms Symes has been moved to energy and resources, the State Electricity Commission, climate action and environment, while remaining the leader of the government in the Legislative Council.
Sonya Kilkenny, who at one stage looked to challenge Mr Carroll for the leadership, remains attorney-general and planning minister, but will also become the new minister for prevention of family violence.
Anthony Carbines hands over the police ministry to Paul Edbrooke, who will also add emergency services, crime prevention and the multicultural affairs portfolio to his swag.
That allows Mr Carbines to take on the new ministry — artificial intelligence and digital economy.
Mr Carroll said Mr Carbines's role would include focusing on ensuring AI developments are ethical and responsible, as well as promoting innovative digital investment.
As part of Mr Carroll's plan to reduce to size of frontbench, Mr Carbines remains the racing minister and leader of the house while taking on major events, medical research and economic development.
A big exclusion from Mr Carroll's government is the transport infrastructure ministry.
The department has a focus of the Labor government for several years, overseeing Victoria's major rail, road, public transport and freight projects including the Metro Tunnel, the Level Crossing Removal Project and the Suburban Rail Loop.
It has previously been filled by Jacinta Allan and most recently by Gabrielle Williams, who became deputy premier under the leadership change.
Ms Williams will be responsible for women and gender equality, skills and training and First Peoples.
She also takes the education portfolio from Mr Carroll as the disruptive industrial relations dispute with the state's public school teachers continues.
New addition to the cabinet Tim Richardson will be the minister for local government, consumer affairs and renters.
